summary.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR12,999 crore on 23% volume growth, while EBITDA margin fell 120 bps QoQ to 13.3%.
summary.overview: Volumes grew 23% YoY and revenue 36%, with an 8% mix benefit plus calibrated price increases driving the gap. Gross margin contracted 300 bps QoQ on about 4.5% net commodity inflation, but cost deferrals and LEAP savings held EBITDA margin to 13.3%. EV volumes rose 151% YoY, with VIDA at 57,000 units in the quarter and capacity being roughly doubled to about 45,000 a month by year-end. Management expects a marginal uptick in input cost inflation in Q2 and says the 14-16% medium-term EBITDA margin target will not be met in the short term.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR50,000 per unit in prior quarter

segments.name: ICE motorcycles and scooters
segments.commentary: ICE volumes grew 21% YoY (18% domestic, 63% global). ICE scooter dispatches almost doubled, with share up 230 bps to close to 7%. 100cc share reached about 86%.

segments.name: EV (VIDA)
segments.commentary: Wholesale grew 151% YoY and share gained more than 400 bps in a year. VIDA quarterly volume was 57,000 units (+26% QoQ), with P&L investment flat at about INR230 crore. Delhi EV share is 16.7%, ranked second.

segments.name: Parts, accessories and apparel (PAM)
segments.commentary: Parts business grew over 30% YoY in Q1 on volume and price. Management expects PAM growth of about 25% or more in FY27, with July trend similar.

segments.name: Global business
segments.commentary: Global volumes grew 63% YoY and exports grew more than 60%, with global market share up 110 bps. Germany ICE launch and VIDA in Nepal were announced.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: marginal uptick in input cost inflation, to be neutralised through mix, discretionary spend cuts and LEAP cost savings.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14-16% retained, but not expected in the short term.
Industry: full-year FY27 growth approaching double digits; H2 growth to be lower YoY due to base effect, but still positive.
EV: capacity to go from about 30,000 to about 45,000 units a month before FY27 end; 100% of EV portfolio PLI-compliant by December 2026.
EV profitability: four-lever plan (scale, BOM cost, LEAP savings, calibrated pricing) with management targeting positive EBITDA by year-end.
Capex: GPC 2.0 parts capacity investment of INR750 crore announced, more than doubling parts handling capacity.
capex_capacity: EV capacity: about 15,000 units a month at FY26 end, about 30,000 in early August, with about 45,000 targeted before FY27 end. Second VIDA phase lands in Q4.
Overall capacity addition of about 2,500 per day across VIDA and ICE scooters; management said about two-thirds is done.
Splendor capacity raised by 2,000 per day (about 50,000+ a month); Destini capacity doubled; Xoom capacity up 50%. Scooter and Splendor additions completed in Q1 or by August 1.
Flex-fuel Splendor and HF Deluxe (E20 to E85) dispatched from third week of July; about 5,000 sold within two weeks in select outlets.
GPC 2.0 parts capex of INR750 crore approved.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler retail (VAHAN) grew 14% YoY in Q1 (ICE +11%, EV +67%); July retail up 28% YoY, with industry growth above 80% in July per management.
Blended ICE price increase of about 4.5% since end-February, with EV per-unit price increases in the early double digits; a marginal ICE price increase was also taken in July.
Tactical price cut on one HF Deluxe variant in select geographies, with immediate demand uplift reported.
Channel inventory: VIDA about 2-3 days; ICE scooter channel stock about half the normal level; motorcycles about 6 weeks, below target.
Retail finance penetration rose to about 65% last month; credit easing is helping demand.
Competition: Hero holds about 86% share of the 100cc segment; management says the category is not at risk from electrification near term.

qa_highlights.question: Demand on the ground for new EV and scooter models, and inventory levels given capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VIDA channel inventory is 2-3 days and retail is immediate; 10,000 more EV capacity comes online in August. ICE scooter channel stock is about half of normal.

qa_highlights.question: How have price hikes been accepted and is 100cc demand stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 100cc share is about 86% and the segment grew from 32% to about 33%. Retail finance penetration reached about 65% last month.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 14-16% this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of returning to the 14-16% range in the medium term, not the short term. The focus is absolute EBITDA growth through volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV revenue share and EV profitability path?
qa_highlights.answer: EV revenue was about INR660 crore, about 5% of Q1 revenue. PLI covers 60% of EV portfolio now and 100% by December. EV EBITDA loss per unit fell from about INR50,000 to INR40,000.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for H2 industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 growth to be positive but lower YoY due to the high base from post-GST sales last year. Full-year industry growth is planned at approaching double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the HF Deluxe price cut taken and what is the premium pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: A tactical cut on one HF Deluxe variant in select geographies lifted demand immediately. Premium refreshes come before the festive season; larger body-change models come in later quarters.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from West Asia-driven commodity and freight inflation; Q2 input cost inflation expected to rise marginally.
EV profitability: EBITDA loss per unit still about INR40,000; 14-16% margin target deferred in the short term.
Market share: a Q1 VAHAN share decline of about 150 bps was raised by an analyst; 125cc and above categories are growing faster than the 100cc segment.
Sustainability of pricing, given cumulative ~4.5% ICE price hikes and a July increase, against volume growth.
Execution of EV capacity ramp to about 45,000 units a month by year-end and of the second VIDA capacity phase in Q4.
Delhi EV policy from FY28 and the timing of new EV motorcycle platforms (not before FY28 per management).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and volume momentum, with a noticeably cautious tone on margins: management said the 14-16% EBITDA margin range will not return in the short term. Answers on EV profitability and motorcycle platforms were more general, without firm numbers.
key_quotes: So a lot of our growth now as well as going forward, you will see in revenue is on top of volume growth, which is contributed by increasing shift to these higher -value products of scooter, premium, EV, and global businesses.
So as we indicated, 14% to 16% is our guidance for the midterm.
So we are confident of mitigating the impact of any potential material price inflation during the quarter through these initiatives.

growth.why: Management guides industry FY27 growth approaching double digits with H2 still positive, backed by specific EV capacity going from about 30,000 to 45,000 a month before FY27 end, Splendor capacity up 2,000 a day, and price/mix gains; the brief gives no company volume guidance, and the FY27 EV capacity target is for year-end.
